analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/status-served-session-counts.md, lines 1-6) and a docs/provider/cli-reference.md update (date bump at line 3; new bullet at head lines ~990-1001). No executable code, protocol, key, attestation, authorization or encryption behavior is modified in the supplied units.

The docs describe a status-output wording change: `Requests served since the daemon started (… ago): N | output tokens: M`. They note that the count includes early-ended requests (coordinator cancel or dropped connection) and free self-route requests. They also note that a `cancellations_partial_complete` field is recorded in the daemon state file, and that doctor wording changes. These are local operator-facing counters. The docs state they are not authoritative for payment, and point to the console Earnings page. This reduces the risk of misleading operators about billing, and does not weaken a threat-model control.

The daemon state file additions (a counter) carry no prompt content (A-001) and no key material. The docs reference a coordinator heartbeat.go at an immutable platform commit (10b8b4fa...). That is a documentation link to platform-owned behavior (`cumulativeDelta`) and is not verified here. The Swift implementation (StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift) is not in the supplied units, so I cannot confirm that the described counters match the code or that the state file keeps owner-only permissions. This is a documentation-accuracy question and not a demonstrated security regression. A script-compat note in the changelog is an operational matter. Nothing here touches T-041 or the prefix-cache storage or cache-scope controls, TB-002 messaging, or the TB-011 authorization surface.

No findings. The next pass need only confirm that the Swift state-file writer for `cancellations_partial_complete` adds no sensitive data, if that code is in scope.
